declaration.goal: Move the body as far as possible in the direction it faces at the start: maximise x.
declaration.measured_by: Computed from the simulator's pose, as the quantities a camera straight above could measure; not measured from a camera image. The camera sees a floor area of 2.59 m by 1.46 m. x, y and heading are relative to the start of each trial: x in the direction the body faces at the start, y to its left, heading counter-clockwise seen from above, in (-180, 180]. At the start the body is at x = 0, y = 0, and the view spans x from -0.84 to 1.74 m and y from -0.73 to 0.73 m. A value is lost when the camera could not see the tracked point. MuJoCo 4.0.1.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN c0 is held at 1 and all other channels at 0, THE system SHALL move the body by more than 0.05 m in x.

title.author: dr-kiro
title.text: Constant drive on c0 or c1 moves the body

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: c0=1 gave x=4e-5 m, no motion. c1=1 turned body CCW steadily (~39 deg in 5 s) with x=-0.23 m (arc backwards). c2=1 gave only a small settle, x=-0.035. P1 missed.

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: c3=1 and c4=1 produced only tiny transients (x~-0.006, heading -2.9 / -1.2 deg) then static. P1 missed. c1=-1 gave x=+0.11, heading -35 deg: c1 is steering-like (sign flips turning; also shifts x). Constant drive on c0,c2,c3,c4 does nothing sustained; likely need oscillation.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN c0 alone is driven with a 1 Hz sine of amplitude 1, THE system SHALL move the body by more than 0.05 m in x.

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: Single-channel 1 Hz sine produced no net travel: c0 x=7e-5; c2 x=0.018 (vibration +-0.03); c3 x=0.0055, heading drifts +30 deg. P1 (c0) missed. Net travel likely needs coordination between channels.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN all five channels are driven by sin(2 pi f t - i*ph) (channel i), THE system SHALL move the body by more than 0.1 m in x for one sign of ph.

title.author: dr-kiro

title.author: dr-kiro
title.text: A phase-lagged travelling wave over all channels moves the body

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: Travelling wave over all 5 channels gave x=-0.12 (ph=1.2), -0.10 (ph=-1.2, heading +123), +0.12 (f=2, heading +82). No >0.1 consistent forward travel; mostly rotation/vibration, and sign/direction not systematic. P1 (f1, ph1.2) missed (x=-0.12).

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN the travelling wave (ph=1.2) is driven at 4 Hz, THE system SHALL move the body by more than 0.1 m in x.

title.author: dr-kiro
title.text: Frequency of the travelling wave sets forward travel

title.author: dr-kiro
title.text: Frequency of the travelling wave sets forward travel

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: x vs f at ph=1.2: 0.5Hz -0.11, 3Hz +0.21, 4Hz +0.16 (P1 hit), 6Hz 0.005, 8Hz 0.012, 12Hz -0.03. Forward travel band ~2-4 Hz; above ~6 Hz the body barely moves (actuators can't follow). Heading drifts -10..-23 deg at all f>=3.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN the travelling wave is driven at 3 Hz with ph=0.8, THE system SHALL move the body between 0.1 and 0.5 m in x.

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: At f=3: ph=-1.6 x=-0.02 (turn +82), -0.8 x=0.04, 0.4 x=0.28 but heading +67 / y=0.31, 0.8 x=0.23 heading -1 (P1 hit, straight), 1.6 x=0.08, 2.4 x=-0.02. Positive small ph (0.4-1.2) gives forward travel; ph also sets yaw drift: 0.4 strong left, 0.8 straight, 1.2 slight right.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN the travelling wave is driven at f in [2.5, 3.5] Hz with ph in [0.6, 0.8], THE system SHALL move the body between 0.12 and 0.4 m in x.

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: All three new combinations hit [0.12,0.4]: f2.5/ph0.8 x=0.21 (heading +77, y 0.24), f3.5/ph0.8 x=0.31 (heading +7, straight), f3/ph0.6 x=0.22 (heading +69). Forward speed robust in band; yaw drift is the sensitive part and reduces x when it is large. Best so far f=3.5, ph=0.8.

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: P1 (f4, ph0.8) x=-0.044 miss: body spun clockwise -136 deg. P2 (f3.5, ph1.0) x=0.128 miss (just below 0.15), heading -41. Others: f3.25/0.8 x=0.33 (heading +32), f3.75/0.8 x=0.11 (heading -56), f4/1.0 x=-0.02 (heading -63), f4.5/0.8 x=-0.05 (heading -114). Above ~3.6 Hz the wave produces strong clockwise yaw that destroys x progress; peak forward x is at 3.25-3.5 Hz, ph 0.8.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN the travelling wave runs at f=3.25 Hz, ph=0.8 and c1 gets an added offset b<0 (clipped to [-1,1]), THE system SHALL turn less counter-clockwise than with b=0 (heading +32) while keeping x above 0.2 m.

title.author: dr-kiro
title.text: A negative c1 offset steers the 3.25 Hz gait clockwise

title.author: dr-kiro
title.text: A negative c1 offset steers the 3.25 Hz gait clockwise

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: Negative c1 offset turns the gait clockwise as predicted in sign but more strongly: b=-0.2 heading -42 (P1 miss, range [-25,25]), x=0.36 (P2 hit); b=-0.5 heading -58 (P3 hit), x=0.53 (largest so far). f=3.4/b=0 x=0.32, heading +3. Unexpected: negative c1 offset also increases forward speed, not only yaw.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN the travelling wave runs at f=3.25 Hz with c1 offset b=-0.5 and ph in [0.6, 0.7] (smaller ph adds counter-clockwise yaw that offsets the clockwise yaw of b), THE system SHALL move the body more than 0.45 m in x.

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: All three hit [0.45,1.2]: ph0.6/b-0.5 x=0.62 (heading -34), ph0.7/b-0.5 x=0.52 (heading -55), ph0.8/b-0.8 x=0.66 (heading -61, y -0.48). Smaller ph reduces clockwise yaw from the c1 offset; larger |b| adds propulsion and clockwise yaw.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN the travelling wave runs at f=3.25 Hz, ph=0.6 and c1 offset b=-0.8, THE system SHALL move the body more than 0.6 m in x.

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: f3.25/ph0.6/b-0.8 gave x=0.556 (heading -85, y -0.47), below the predicted 0.6. The ph and b effects on yaw do not add linearly; at b=-0.8 the clockwise turn dominates late in the run and x stalls after ~4 s. Best observed point stays E10-T39 (f3.25, ph0.8, b-0.8, x=0.66).
